title: Deadly Russian drone strike targets apartment in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, killing 3, injuring 12
description: One of the injured victims is an 11-year-old girl. Five wounded individuals are being treated in the hospital, with two in serious condition and undergoing surgery.
content:
A Russian drone hit a residential building in the Synelnykove district of Dnipropetrovsk Oblast on Oct. 24, killing three civilians and injuring another 12, Governor Oleksandr Hanzha reported.
The drone attack caused a fire on the fourth floor of an apartment building and also damaged nearby vehicles and a store, Hanzha said . Three victims were killed.
At least 12 other people were injured in Russia's strike on Synelnykove, according to Hanzha. One of the victims is an 11-year-old girl. Five injured individuals are being treated in the hospital.
Three of the injured victims — two women and one man— are reported to be in serious condition and undergoing surgery.
Lethal Russian drone strikes are a daily occurrence in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast , which borders Ukraine's front-line Kharkiv, Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia, and Kherson oblasts. The region's Synelnykove district has endured frequent attacks, active fighting, and temporary incursions by Russian troops due to its proximity to Russian-occupied territory.
In October 2026, Russia has intensified aerial bombardments across Ukraine in its annual attempt to destroy the country's power grid as temperatures drop. Thousands of homes in Synelnykove and other parts of Dnipropetrovsk Oblast lost power after Russia attacked the region's critical energy infrastructure overnight on Oct. 21.

title: Ukrainian forces reportedly strike Russian targets 2,500 kilometers from border
description: Ukraine struck several targets, including a petrochemical plant and a warehouse in Siberia around 2,500 kilometers away from the border on Oct. 24, monitoring channels reported.
content:
Editor's note: This is a developing story and is being updated.
Ukraine struck several targets, including a petrochemical plant and a warehouse in Siberia around 2,500 kilometers away from the border on Oct. 24, monitoring channels reported.
A fire first broke out at the Omsky Kauchuk petrochemical plant in the Russian city of Omsk, according to Ukrainian monitoring channel Exilenova Plus.
The facility is one of Russia's largest petrochemical plants, and the company behind Omsky Kauchuk says the site is a leading producer of synthetic rubber, organic synthesis products, and methyl tert-butyl ether, an additive used to refine gasoline.
The plant is part of Russia's supply chain for rocket fuel, including for the Iskander ballistic missile used in fatal attacks against Ukraine, Exilenova Plus said.
Russian ballistic missiles targeted Kyiv in a fatal attack on the night of Oct. 13-14, killing five people and injuring another 25. At least one person was killed, and 24 were injured in another Russian ballistic missile attack overnight on Oct. 22.
Later, a warehouse belonging to major Russian online retailer Ozon was also hit in the Ukrainian drone attack, Exilenova Plus reported .
Omsk Oblast Governor Vitaliy Khotsenko confirmed that the region was targeted by Ukrainian drones, saying that a logistics hub in the city of Omsk was hit.
"A logistics hub in Omsk was attacked by a drone. Personnel were promptly evacuated. Emergency services are working at the scene," he claimed.
Reports could not be immediately verified by the Kyiv Independent.
Ozon and its competitor Wildberries have been targeted by Ukrainian forces in recent months. The two are a major part of Russia's economy, with their broader ecosystems accounting for about 8.5% of Russia's GDP.
Ukraine has targeted facilities that often serve as storage sites for dual-use goods used in weapons production and other military purposes.
Ukraine regularly strikes military targets deep within Russia and occupied territories in an effort to diminish Moscow's ability to continue waging its war.
Omsk Oblast was also under fire in an attack on Oct. 8. Ukraine's General Staff confirmed that its forces struck the Omsk oil refinery .
"The destruction of such facilities is the exercise by Ukraine of its inalienable right to self-defense in accordance with Article 51 of the UN Charter and is aimed at reducing the military-economic potential of the Russian Federation," Ukraine's General Staff said .
More recently, on Oct. 24, the General Staff said that Ukrainian forces struck the Tolyattikauchuk petrochemical plant in the Russian city of Tolyatti, Samara Oblast, as well as an aircraft at the Yeysk airfield in Krasnodar Krai.
The synthetic rubbers are used to make solid rocket fuel for tactical and ballistic missiles, according to the General Staff.
"Damage to such objects affects the supply chain of raw materials for the Russian missile program," Ukraine's General Staff wrote.

title: European Parliament Vice President ends hunger strike following Oleshky ceasefire announcement
description: European Parliament Vice President Pina Picierno announced the hunger strike on Oct. 20, demanding an immediate humanitarian truce in the occupied town.
content:
The European Parliament Vice President Pina Picierno ended her hunger strike, meant to raise awareness for the humanitarian crisis in the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky, Kherson Oblast, following the announcement of a ceasefire agreement, Ukraine's human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets said on Oct. 24.
Lubinets said he informed Picierno that a temporary local ceasefire in Oleshky had been agreed to allow humanitarian aid deliveries and the evacuation of the civilian population starting on Oct. 27. The agreement includes demining the road to the town, deliveries of food, water, medicine, and medical equipment, and the safe passage of civilians, he added.
Some 2,000 civilians remain trapped in Oleshky, located just across the Dnipro River from Kherson , with Russian troops blocking humanitarian aid from entering, despite a critical shortage of food and medicine. Civilians attempting to flee via the mined roads in and out of the city are frequently targeted by drones.
Picierno announced the hunger strike on Oct. 20, demanding an immediate humanitarian truce in the occupied town. "It is time to act together, so that diplomacy delivers concrete results and no one is left to die in silence," she said. Her announcement came days after Pope Leo XIV called for a ceasefire following a phone call with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Oct. 16.
Ukraine will fulfill its part of the "extremely difficult" humanitarian operation, President Volodymyr Zelensky said in a video message on Oct. 24. "We hope that it will be possible to carry out this humanitarian operation — to unblock Oleshky," he added.
The temporary truce was facilitated by U.S. first lady Melania Trump, who spoke with both the Russian and Ukrainian sides.
"Non-military, civilian leaders from both countries will work together to visit Oleshky residents in their homes and determine the level of assistance they require," Melania Trump was quoted as saying in a press release .
"Residents who wish to evacuate will receive coordinated support and transportation to their preferred destination. I anticipate some will want to go to Russia, and some to Ukraine."

title: Germany in talks to buy Ukrainian jet-powered drones
description: The Bars jet powered drone has a range of 1,000 kilometers and can reach speeds of up to 700 kilometers per hour.
content:
Germany is negotiating a deal with Ukraine to purchase Bars jet-powered drones, a German official with knowledge of the matter told the Kyiv Independent on Oct. 24.
Berlin is discussing the deal with Kyiv as Germany plans to buy thousands of deep-strike weapons from European arms companies, as initially reported by Bloomberg on Oct. 23.
According to officials Bloomberg spoke with, Germany’s future strategic thinking involves using masses of cheap missiles to overwhelm enemy air defenses. Currently, Germany’s army only operates midrange Taurus cruise missiles, while the U.S. warned its allies to expect years-long delays for missile deliveries.
The Bars jet powered drone has a range of 1,000 kilometers and can reach speeds of up to 700 kilometers per hour. The manufacturer of the drones is not publicly known for security reasons. The Ukrainian army launches around 2,000 of these drones per month, targeting Russian oil refineries, power plants, and substations, a representative of the company told Ukrainian media outlet NV in September. Germany and Ukraine signed a deal to jointly produce Bars in July 2026 as part of the Build with Ukraine initiative. Under the first stage of the deal, Germany would finance the production of the drones, while all manufactured equipment would be sent to Ukraine’s Armed Forces.
Recently, President Volodymyr Zelensky said that Bars have proven to be one of the most effective interceptors against Russian jet-powered drones, as Moscow escalates attacks on Ukrainian cities, Ukrinform reported on Oct. 10.
Germany has emerged as the biggest foreign partner in Ukraine’s burgeoning defense tech sector. A September report from the Kyiv School of Economics Institute found that there were 36 joint ventures between Ukrainian and German firms, as Berlin prioritizes deep-strike technology and intelligence.

title: Ukraine sanctions Russian arms suppliers as Moscow ramps up attacks
description: Included in the first sanctions list are 51 Russian citizens and 44 businesses producing and supplying raw materials, equipment, and tools used in long-range weapons like Iskander, Kalibr, Kh-101, and Kinzhal missiles.
content:
President Volodymyr Zelensky imposed new sanctions on Russian citizens and companies helping produce ballistic missiles, aircraft, armored vehicles, and drones, the President’s Office announced on Oct. 24.
Included in the first sanctions list are 51 Russian citizens and 44 businesses producing and supplying raw materials, equipment, and tools used in long-range weapons like Iskander, Kalibr, Kh-101, and Kinzhal missiles.
A second sanctions list targets 32 Russian citizens and 35 companies involved in the production and supply chains of equipment and components used in Russia’s military-industrial complex.
"We are systematically identifying and imposing sanctions on enterprises involved in producing Russian ballistic missiles and other weapons. We are working to extend these sanctions to other jurisdictions," said Ukraine’s sanctions chief, Vladyslav Vlasiuk.
"Together, these measures should significantly weaken the Russian military-industrial complex's ability to produce weapons."
In particular, Ukraine targeted Russia's RUSAL Group, a key company involved in the production of military aircraft, armored vehicles, missile weapons, and drones. The company imported 150 million rubles ($1.8 million) worth of aluminum oxide between April 2024 and March 2025, which supplied Russia's military-industrial complex, the President's Office said.
The sanctions come as Russia ramps up its production of missiles and drones. Ukrainian intelligence (HUR) told Ukrainian media earlier this week that Russia produces some 10,000 drones per month and is currently stockpiling 700 ballistic missiles.
As Russia scales up arms production, attacks on Ukrainian cities, particularly Kyiv, have reached unprecedented levels. Civilian casualties are currently at levels not seen in over four years.
Last month, Russia killed at least 328 civilians and injured 2,105 — the deadliest September since the start of the full-scale invasion, and 85% higher than September 2025, the United Nations Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine reported on Oct. 15.

title: Russian attacks kill 4, injure 78 across Ukraine over past day, as drone strikes Kyiv residential building in the morning
description: Overnight, Russian forces launched 126 drones, 61 of which were jet-powered, while Ukraine's air defense managed to suppress 101 drones, including 50 jet-powered drones, the Air Force said.
content:
Russian attacks over the last day killed four people and injured 78 across Ukraine over the past day, as Moscow strikes at Kyiv in the morning of Oct. 24, local authorities report.
In the early hours of Oct. 24, a Russian drone struck a residential building in Kyiv’s Obolon District, injuring two people, and cauing a fire, the Kyiv City Military Administration reported .
On Oct. 23, Russian forces attacked the city of Chernihiv in Chernihiv Oblast during the day, killing one man and injuring at least 25 people, local authorities said.
An air raid alert was declared in Chernihiv at around 1:40 p.m. local time due to a missile threat. Minutes later, Ukraine's Air Force reported drones and a Banderol low-cost cruise missile heading toward the city.
Chernihiv City Council said two private businesses were targeted in the Russian attack but provided no further details.
In Donetsk Oblast , Russian shelling of a residential area in the front-line city of Kramatorsk killed one person and injured six more, including three children, the Donetsk Oblast Prosecutor's Office reported on Oct. 23.
In Sloviansk , another front-line town in Donetsk Oblast, Russian attacks throughout the previous day killed one 62-year-old woman and injured four people, Sloviansk Mayor Vadym Lyakh wrote on Oct. 24.
In Dnipropetrovsk Oblast , a Russian attack on the city of Dnipro killed one and injured eight people, while three more people were injured in the Pidhorodnenska community, according to regional governor Oleksandr Hanzha .
In Zhytomyr Oblast , a Russian drone attack in the city of Zhytomyr injured nine people on Oct. 23, including two children, Ukraine’s police force reported .
In Kharkiv Oblast , Russian forces injured seven people, including a 12-year-old girl and a 13-year-old boy, Kharkiv Oblast Governor Oleh Synehubov said. Homes, businesses, and gas stations were also damaged or destroyed in the strikes, he added.
In Kherson Oblast , Russian forces struck residential areas across the region, injuring six people on Oct. 23, the Kherson Oblast Military Administration reported.
In Ukraine's southern Odesa Oblast , three people were injured in Russian attacks over the past day, as Russia struck a recreational building, an administrative building, and a warehouse, said regional governor Oleh Kiper .
In Sumy Oblast , Russia carried out 40 attacks on 25 settlements, injuring five people in several communities over the past day, the regional military administration said. In total, the air alert sounded for more than 18 hours, the administration added.
Overnight, Russian forces launched 126 drones, 61 of which were jet-powered, Ukraine’s Air Force reported . Ukraine managed to suppress 101 drones, including 50 jet-powered drones, the Air Force said. Russia ramped up production of jet-powered drones this year, which are much harder to shoot down than their propeller powered predecessors, while Ukraine has managed to improve the interception rate over the last month.

title: Ukraine strikes factory in Russia's Tolyatti, airfield in Krasnodar Krai, General Staff says
description: Videos filmed by locals show smoke billowing over the city in the early morning, with reports claiming that the Tolyattikauchuk chemical plant was attacked and that evacuations took place at the AvtoVAZ car manufacturing factory.
content:
Ukrainian forces struck the Tolyattikauchuk plant in the Russian city of Tolyatti, Samara Oblast, as well as an aircraft at the Yeysk airfield in Krasnodar Krai, Ukraine’s General Staff said on Oct. 24.
The General Staff said it recorded an explosion and a fire in the area of the Tolyattikauchuk plant. The plant produces synthetic rubbers, monomers, and high-octane gasoline additives. According to the General Staff, the synthetic rubbers are used to make solid rocket fuel for tactical and ballistic missiles.
"Damage to such objects affects the supply chain of raw materials for the Russian missile program," the General Staff added.
Telegram monitoring channels reported earlier in the day that fires broke out at several plants and factories in Tolyatti amid a wave of drone attacks overnight.
Videos filmed by locals show smoke billowing over the city in the early morning, with reports claiming that the Tolyattikauchuk chemical plant was attacked and that evacuations took place at the AvtoVAZ car manufacturing factory.
Ukrainian Telegram channel Exilenova+ also claimed that a "military-purpose plant" was on fire, although without specifying what the plant produced.
Located around 1,300 kilometers from Kyiv, Tolyatti has been targeted by Ukraine on several occasions, including attacks on the Tolyattikauchuk rubber plant on Sept. 12 and the Tolyattikauchuk chemical plant and KuibyshevAzot chemical plants on April 4.
Ukrainian forces also struck an aircraft at the Yeysk airfield, the General Staff said, while the extent of the damage is still undetermined clarified. The General Staff did not specify the type of aircraft damaged in the attack.
The Kyiv Independent could not independently verify the claims.
In recent months, both Russia and Ukraine have ramped up attacks on businesses and enterprises. Kyiv’s long-range drone campaign has targeted numerous companies helping Russia’s war effort, while Moscow has taken a no-limits approach, destroying food logistics hubs, postal services, and public transport, killing numerous civilians in the process.

title: The trouble with loving Russia: Evan Gershkovich's memoir seeks sentimentality in a lost country
